notes.title: Introducing Reveka and Craita
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769072/30c9524533ec86943d179d12f1e932965ab0ea0e.png[/img]

[h3]REVEKA[/h3]

Reveka is an influential and enigmatic vampire whose past intertwines deeply with Vorago’s legacy. Once known for her cunning charm and sophisticated allure, she has a long history marked by seduction, manipulation, and tragedy. When the Inquisition attacked Vorago’s castle, Reveka fled to the mines, pursued by Inquisitors. In a moment of desperate fury, Reveka unleashed elemental flames that turned the northern territories of Sangavia into a scorched landscape known as Hell’s Chasm.

Reveka finds herself facing unresolved anger, regret, and an insatiable desire for vengeance. Initially cautious and skeptical, she tests Dragos strength and loyalty, ultimately seeking his assistance in confronting her past…

If the player earns Reveka’s trust, she joins Dragos' cause, operating as both a trader and a tax collector in Hell’s Chasm. She provides significant amounts of gold and rare dark artifacts; her involvement is crucial for reclaiming the devastated land and establishing dominance over the region.
 
[h3]CRAITA[/h3]
Craita is a powerful figure deeply connected to nature and primal forces. She leads the Grove of Wisdom, a cult centered around worshipping a sacred tree revered as a living bridge between humans and earth spirits. Renowned for her profound knowledge of healing and herbs, Craita is considered an extraordinarily skilled healer. She possesses a calm yet authoritative presence, capable of inspiring both reverence and fear among her followers.

When the Pale Soarer, a terrifying beast, begins attacking villagers, Craita faces an internal crisis. Some of her followers perceive this creature as a divine force and secretly begin worshipping it, an act Craita regards as a betrayal of their beliefs. Resolute in her convictions, she seeks Dragos aid to purge these fanatics from her community.

If the player earns Craita’s trust, she will function as both a trader and a tax collector in the Grove of Wisdom, providing valuable potions, resources, and knowledge crucial to restoring the land.

notes.title: Rumour has it
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769072/b85523620bdf7db50c8ef67d5870d0944a5275cd.png[/img]

What are Rumours?

As you explore villages in your dual role, you’ll uncover a powerful mechanic: Rumours. These fragments of gossip, secrets, and speculation tell you more than idle chatter—they help you predict what role a villager will best fulfill once you grant them the Kiss of Eternity and turn them into a vampire.

Not all villagers are created equally in undeath. Some are better suited as spies, others as warriors or scholars. Rumours give you the insight to build a stronger vampiric court, tailored to your strategy.
Switching Roles: Aristocrat and Hunter

You can toggle between two modes:
[list]
[*] As the Hunter, you stalk prey and use brute force to achieve your goals.
[*] As the Aristocrat, you walk among the people and gather Rumours.
[/list]

Only in Aristocrat mode can you collect these critical insights. Engage with villagers, listen to their stories, and extract the truths buried in small talk.

Why does it matter?

Your power grows not just through blood, but through careful selection and planning. The villagers you choose to elevate with the Kiss of Eternity will define the future of your domain. Choose wisely.

notes.title: Vampire Dynasty - Applied construction law for vampires
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769072/8bbbb232896d9e1b3262abca444f050568af3b26.jpg[/img]

Building a castle is a large and complex undertaking that requires careful planning and expertise. Here is some advice for someone looking to tackle this ambitious project:

1. Detailed planning - Define goals, but don't wait until sunrise!
2. Hire an architect and experts - make sure you have a sufficient supply of blood.
3. Site selection and land - Already developed land is no obstacle. You are a vampire!
4 Permits and regulations - Write in ink, blood is too valuable!
5 Design and functionality - The latter for the crypt, the former for the gusto!
6. Building materials and construction - Only use high-quality materials and do-it-yourself!
7. Project management - schedules are very important. Sunrise and sunset, right?!
8. Safety - Have we mentioned the sun yet?
9. Furnishings and decoration - Only the best!
10. Maintenance - vampire hunters and the evil sun, always take precautions!
Bonus: Legal and Financial Advice - Occasionally raid the village treasury!

More information in the video!

[previewyoutube=BIL6j7tjD8w;full][/previewyoutube]

Please let us know your impressions of the demo! Message us here on the Steam forum or on our social media channels! We also just realised that your wishlist could use some blood!

Until the next dawn, may the moon guide you safely.

notes.title: Vampire Dynasty – Wooden stakes & answers #1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769072/1181df61b8fe391df9e17073cb4b31152b7afb1d.png[/img]

We have just received an urgent despatch from Sangavia!

[i]Thank you for all your questions regarding Vampire Dynasty. 

You asked! We answer! Let’s Go![/i]

[previewyoutube=qqp0aUI8y10;full][/previewyoutube]



Here is the script for your convenience!

[h3]How big is the team working on the title?[/h3]
[i]20 people are currently working on the Vampire Dynasty. The largest part is the 3D art department, which has 5 people. Additionally we have 3 programmers, 2 level designers, 2 animators, 2 concept artists, 2 internal testers, a CEO,  one sound designer, a producer, a composer and a sound designer/composer. As for the game design, many of the people mentioned have a hand in it, but its up to the lead designer and CEO to wrap it up into a coherent piece and outline the direction.[/i]

[h3]How would you describe the ratio of story content to sandbox and open world content?[/h3]
[i]In terms of story, it is extremely difficult to tell a satisfying story in a pure sandbox formula. In Vampire Dynasty, we play a defined character in a defined world. We meet NPCs who have their own backstories and aspirations. But, of course, the players can influence this world and explore it at will to uncover its secrets. And most of all - this approach to the plot allows for some heavy moral choices, which we have a lot of in the game.[/i]

[h3]What can I build? [/h3]
[i]The players focus on building a castle, including chambers and work stations for the dynasty members, and prisons for the thralls. The players can influence every element of the castle, from the type of the walls to the patterns that can be painted on them. 
All this is done to give the players absolute creative freedom.[/i]

[h3]How do you add people to your vampire "clan" or "family"?[/h3]
[i]The higher your dynasty level, the more NPCs you can transform. Except for plot characters and vampire hunters, you can bestow the Kiss of Eternity on any resident of Sangavia, who will then turn into a child of the night and serve faithfully in your castle. [/i]

[h3]Can I get command or torture thralls to get myself into a better position?[/h3]
[i]The players can expand their influence not only by turning people into vampires, but also by abducting humans and keeping them in the castle. Imprisoning thralls in order to frequently obtain blood from them is a simple way to make the existence as a vampire easier. [/i]

[h3]Will I be able to change the appearance of my character throughout the gameplay?[/h3]
[i]You will be able to influence the appearance of your character by choosing the outfit. As for a wider change of appearance - we would like to introduce this, but we don't know at what stage we will be able to do it - if at all. But we will look into that. [/i]

[h3]Is leveling based on experience or gear?[/h3]
[i]A character's advancement is determined by the level of their dynasty. The players increase it by progressing the story line or completing quests related to the castle development. The higher the dynasty level is, the higher the capabilities of the characters are. Higher dynasty status gives the players access to new items to build and most importantly - allows them to create more vampires. 
Equipment found while exploring also increases the capabilities of your character. Importantly, in the game we have two outfit types, which the players can alternate between. When wearing the aristocrat’s attire, the character pretends to be a noble person who manages local lands. And as a hunter, they can hunt without fear of being detected.[/i]

[h3]Is the game combat heavy?[/h3]
[i]Absolutely not... if you don't want it to be. 
You play as Dragos, who, in addition to being a vampire, is the ruler of the surrounding lands. There is a village around the castle where his peasants live. The players can treat them well as benevolent aristocrats, supporting their livelihood and, from time to time, drinking the blood of the dangerous or sickly Medresti residents. They can also... murder whoever they want. The choice is theirs.
In creating the Vampire Dynasty, we want the players to feel that they are at the top of the food chain. As a result, fighting average people is not demanding at all. However, the situation gets more complicated when your bold actions attract the attention of vampire hunters.[/i]

[h3]Can I travel as a bat across the whole map?[/h3]
[i]Vampire Dynasty was inspired by the mythology and the pop culture associated with the vampires, keeping some elements and adapting others in a creative way. One of those elements is the transformation into a bat, which... isn't really a transformation at all.
Vampires once ruled Sangavia, and during their era many artifacts were created that combined magic and science. One of these artifacts were bat statues, which the players can bring to life and control with blood. 
In this way, the players can explore the area around the statue, getting into places that were not accessible from the ground. This mechanic is used for minor puzzles that are scattered around the world. [/i]

[h3]Does the game convey the incredible powers (and weaknesses) of a vampire?[/h3]
[i]The vampires in Sangavia are much stronger and much more agile than an average human, and they are immortal. Unfortunately, the light of the sun burns their pale skin and they need blood to survive. Players won't have to worry about garlic or whether someone has invited them into their home - which doesn't mean the game can't feature vampire clans that have such restrictions. [/i]

[h3]How does Vampire Dynasty differ from other Dynasty games?[/h3]
[i]For the first time we are dealing with a game that breaks out of historical realities and introduces a fantasy element. Second of all - our building system is significantly different - after all, you aren’t building a village, but one big castle, which can look just the way we dreamt of. Last but not least - we put a lot of attention into the story aspect. If the story doesn't interest you, go ahead and focus on building, exploring, gathering resources, or hunting. But if you're planning on soaking up the story, we've got you covered with a plot full of well-rounded characters, plot twists, and tough choices. And it's all available in co-op.[/i]

That’s it! Keep the questions coming!

See you soon for more information about Vampire Dynasty!
